trace.reasoning: The ECG shows a regular rhythm with visible P waves preceding each QRS complex, indicating sinus origin. The rate is elevated, consistent with sinus tachycardia. This supports option E. The closest alternative, atrial fibrillation (C), is ruled out by the presence of organized P waves and regular rhythm, whereas AFib presents with an irregularly irregular rhythm and absent P waves.
